compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Commit 9ba1e90 (bug 330c, "box flips no longer stale attestations") changed the material-fingerprint algorithm in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py::material_fingerprint` to normalize AC checkbox state (`[x]` -> `[ ]`) before hashing — but with NO grandfathering of attestations signed under the OLD (non-normalized) algorithm. `compute_validity` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`) recomputes the CURRENT fingerprint with the new algorithm and compares it to the `material:` hash frozen in the signed manifest. Every completion attestation signed pre-330c embeds `[x]` in its hash basis (the 433c close gate REQUIRES all boxes checked at close), so after 330c landed those attestations read `stale-material` ("materially edited since the completion verdict") even though the ticket never changed.

Observed blast radius: epic 2f4c-7e5c-e782-4e97 closed 2026-08-03 with a PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT but NO signed completion attestation — `child_closure_findings` (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py`) read 4 pre-330c children (433c, 9d07, a584, d3ed) as closed-but-uncertified, `gate_ops.completion_precheck` set `certifiable=False`, and `transition_close.py` (the `certifiable is False` early return) silently skipped signing. Proof: each of those children's signed `material:` hash equals a byte-exact recomputation with the LEGACY non-normalized basis, while post-330c child 1e95 matches the normalized recomputation. This violates 330c's own AC ("existing attestations ... remain valid" — backward compatibility) and the epic-level verdict-trust design (a child validly certified at close must keep counting).

## Approach
Validity-on-read grandfathering, no event mutation: where `compute_validity` compares the signed `material:` fingerprint against `current_material_fingerprint`, on mismatch ALSO recompute the fingerprint over the legacy (non-normalized) basis and accept an exact legacy match as not-materially-edited. A legacy match means the basis (description including box state, file_impact, children) is byte-identical to what was signed, which is strictly stronger than the normalized check — no weakening. Apply to both the completion-verifier and plan-review branches (same seam, same class). Additionally make the certifiable=False unsigned-close path observable: carry `certifiable` on the PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar payload and warn on stderr when a PASS close is left unsigned because certification was withheld (today it is fully silent, which is what forced this archaeology).

## Scope
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py (legacy fingerprint variant)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py (compute_validity: legacy fallback on mismatch)
- src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py (PASS payload carries certifiable)
- src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py (stderr warning on certifiable=False unsigned close)
- tests/unit (RED-first regression tests)

## Testing
RED first: a completion attestation whose manifest `material:` was computed WITHOUT checkbox normalization over a checked description must read valid=True from compute_validity (fails today with stale-material); a genuinely edited description must still read stale-material (negative control); the PASS sidecar payload must carry certifiable; the unsigned certifiable=False close path must emit a stderr warning.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A completion attestation signed under the pre-330c (non-normalized) fingerprint over an unchanged ticket reads valid/certified from compute_validity.
- [ ] A plan-review attestation signed under the pre-330c fingerprint over an unchanged ticket is likewise not invalidated as stale-material.
- [ ] A real material edit (text change) still invalidates: legacy fallback does not weaken staleness detection.
- [ ] The PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar records the verdict's certifiable flag.
- [ ] A PASS close that skips signing because certifiable=False warns on stderr (no longer silent).
